ERR-EL-001.component_group: Exhaust System â€” Manifold-to-Head Gasket Assembly
ERR-EL-001.mechanical_failure_mode: Failed manifold-to-head gasket admits air into exhaust stream between cylinder pulses via venturi effect. Upstream O2 reads false-lean, driving positive fuel trim. CO2 stays near normal â€” combustion is stoichiometric; only the sample is diluted by the leak.
ui_remediation_steps: Cold-engine listening test: a ticking/chuffing sound from the manifold-to-head area that diminishes as the engine warms (metal expansion closes the gap) is the hallmark of a manifold gasket leak.
Use an exhaust gas analyser probe near each manifold runner-to-head junction â€” HC detection at the joint confirms escaping combustion gas before the O2 sensor.
Inspect all manifold gasket faces for carbon soot trails or visible blowout marks.
Perform a smoke test via the tailpipe with the engine off â€” smoke escaping at the manifold-to-head joint confirms the leak path.
Replace the failed exhaust manifold gasket. Inspect the manifold flange for flatness â€” a warped flange will cause the new gasket to fail within weeks.
Verify repair: O2 sensor switching pattern normalises at 2500 RPM, fuel trims return to within Â±10 %, cross-counts â‰¥ 8 in 10 seconds.

ERR-EL-002.component_group: Exhaust System â€” Exhaust Manifold Assembly
impacted_subsystems: Exhaust Manifold (Cast Iron or Tubular Steel)
ERR-EL-002.mechanical_failure_mode: Crack in cast-iron or tubular-steel manifold opens under thermal cycling, admitting air pre-O2 sensor. Cast-iron cracks from thermal shock; tubular headers crack at weld stress risers. Leak is pulse-synchronous and louder when cold before expansion closes the gap.
ui_remediation_steps: Cold-engine start: listen for a loud, sharp ticking that is synchronised with cylinder firing (half engine speed). The noise should diminish or disappear as the manifold heats up and the crack closes.
Spray a small amount of soapy water near suspected crack points with the engine running cold â€” exhaust gas bubbling through the solution confirms the crack location.
Exhaust analyser probe: sniff each manifold runner for HC trace at the suspected crack point.
Remove the exhaust manifold heatshield (if fitted) and visually inspect for carbon trails radiating from the crack â€” a black soot line tracing from the fracture confirms the leak.
Cast-iron manifolds can sometimes be welded by a specialist; replacement is the standard repair. Replace flange gaskets and hardware as part of the job.
Verify repair: after manifold replacement or weld, O2 sensor switching returns to normal, fuel trims stabilise within Â±10 %, no exhaust noise.

ERR-EL-003.component_group: Exhaust System â€” Manifold-to-Downpipe Flange Joint
impacted_subsystems: Pre-Catalyst O2 Sensor (if sensor is downstream of the flange)
ERR-EL-003.mechanical_failure_mode: Bolted flange between manifold outlet and downpipe/cat develops gasket leak. NA engines with O2 in manifold: leak is post-O2 (noise, no trim). Turbo engines with O2 in downpipe: pre-O2 dilution drives false-lean correction and delayed spool from exhaust pressure loss.
ui_remediation_steps: Cold-engine listening: a sharp metallic ticking at the manifold-to-downpipe flange joint. The noise is loudest at the joint â€” use a mechanic's stethoscope or hose to isolate.
Exhaust analyser probe: sniff the flange joint area for HC trace. If the O2 sensor is downstream of the leak, expect false-lean trim offset (positive LTFT).
Inspect the flange hardware â€” loose or missing bolts, or a visibly displaced gasket, are common on vehicles with a history of exhaust work.
If the gasket has failed, replace the flange gasket. Check the flange faces for flatness â€” pitting or warping requires resurfacing.
On turbo vehicles: check that the leak has not caused the turbo to overspeed (compensating for lost exhaust energy). Verify wastegate actuator stroke after repair.
Verify repair: no exhaust noise at the flange, O2 sensor behaviour normal (if applicable), turbo spool within specification.

ERR-EL-004.component_group: Exhaust System â€” Flex Pipe Section (Downstream of Catalyst)
impacted_subsystems: Tailpipe Emission Sampling (probe downstream of the leak)
ERR-EL-004.mechanical_failure_mode: Stainless-steel flex bellows (post-cat) ruptures from engine rocking, corrosion, or impact. Post-cat and post-O2 â€” no fuel trim disturbance. Primary symptoms: exhaust noise and cabin fume entry. Check engine mounts: excessive movement causes repeat failure.
ui_remediation_steps: Start the engine and listen for a loud exhaust rumble or blatting noise from underneath the vehicle, typically near the flex section location (forward of the centre resonator).
Have an assistant hold a rag over the tailpipe with the engine running â€” listen for hissing at the flex pipe as exhaust gas escapes through the rupture instead of exiting the tailpipe.
Visually inspect the flex pipe braiding for broken wires, rust-through, carbon soot marks, or visible tears in the bellows.
Check engine mounts before replacing the flex pipe â€” excessive engine movement is the root cause of repeated flex pipe failure.
Replace the flex pipe section (cut-and-weld or bolt-in depending on the vehicle). Ensure the replacement has adequate flexibility for the vehicle's engine movement range.
Verify repair: no exhaust noise from the flex section, tailpipe sample unaffected, no cabin fumes during stationary operation.

ERR-EL-005.component_group: Exhaust System â€” EGR Feed Tube Assembly
impacted_subsystems: EGR Feed Tube (Exhaust Manifold to EGR Valve)
Upstream O2 Sensor (false-lean from pre-O2 leak)
ERR-EL-005.mechanical_failure_mode: EGR feed tube (manifold to EGR valve) develops crack or pinhole at weld or flex section. Exhaust escapes before EGR valve, reducing flow. Pre-O2: venturi air ingress drives false-lean O2 readings. Post-O2: noise and reduced EGR flow without fuel trim disturbance.
ui_remediation_steps: Listen for a ticking noise near the EGR tube routing path. The noise is often quieter than a manifold leak because the tube diameter is smaller.
Inspect the EGR feed tube visually for carbon soot marks, rust-through, or cracks at the corrugated flex section and at the flare nut connections.
If the leak is pre-O2: check LTFT for positive offset from false-lean correction. Post-O2: no trim effect â€” diagnose by noise and visual inspection.
Replace the EGR feed tube. Ensure the new tube is correctly torqued at both flare nuts â€” over-tightening cracks the flare; under-tightening leaks.
After replacement, clear DTCs and verify the EGR monitor completes during a drive cycle without setting P0401 (insufficient flow) or P0402 (excessive flow).
Verify repair: no exhaust noise, LTFT within Â±10 % (if pre-O2), EGR monitor passes.

ERR-EL-006.component_group: Exhaust System â€” Slip-Joint or Flange Compression Seal
ERR-EL-006.mechanical_failure_mode: Graphite or metal-core donut gasket at slip-joint or spring-bolted flange deteriorates from heat cycling, losing compression seal. Joint opens under load when exhaust flexes, causing dilution or noise. Common at manifold-to-downpipe, downpipe-to-cat, cat-to-catback joints.
ui_remediation_steps: Load the engine against the torque converter (foot firmly on brake, brief throttle in Drive) and listen for an exhaust blat at the suspect joint â€” the joint opens under load when the engine rocks.
Visually inspect the donut gasket at each flange connection. Look for carbon soot tracks radiating from the flange, a deformed or flattened gasket, or broken spring bolts.
If the joint uses spring-loaded bolts, verify both springs are intact and have not lost tension â€” a broken spring bolt allows the joint to open under engine movement.
Replace the donut gasket. Replace spring bolts and springs as a set if any are broken or corroded.
Apply a thin layer of high-temperature exhaust assembly paste to the new donut if specified by the vehicle manufacturer.
Verify repair: no exhaust noise at the joint under load, no carbon soot track re-formation, tailpipe sample integrity maintained.

ERR-EL-008.component_group: Exhaust System — Post-Catalyst Exhaust Leak and Tailpipe Sampling Integrity
ERR-EL-008.mechanical_failure_mode: Severe post-catalyst exhaust leak or sampling-probe seal failure contaminating the gas analyser sample with ambient air. The sum-of-gases check (CO+CO2+O2) falls outside the 14-18% validation window, producing a SAMPLE_INVALID verdict from GASLab. The chemistry is unclassifiab...
ui_remediation_steps: Verify the gas analyser sampling probe is fully inserted into the tailpipe and the probe cone or stopper seals against the tailpipe opening. A loose probe is the most common cause of SAMPLE_INVALID.
Check for visible exhaust leaks downstream of the catalyst: look for carbon soot marks at muffler seams, pipe joints, and the tailpipe-to-muffler connection.
With the engine running, have an assistant hold a rag over the tailpipe to create backpressure — listen for hissing at any downstream joint that indicates an exhaust gas escape path.
If a post-catalyst leak is confirmed: replace the failed gasket, clamp, or pipe section. Post-catalyst leaks do not affect O2 sensor or fuel trim, but they do corrupt the gas sample.
Run the gas analyser calibration verification routine on a known reference gas before re-testing — a drifted analyser can produce a SAMPLE_INVALID verdict on a perfectly valid sample.
Verify repair: CO+CO2+O2 sum returns to within 14-18% window, GASLab sample_validity returns VALID, gas analyser chemistry is classifiable.

ERR-EL-007.component_group: Exhaust System — Pre-O2 Sensor Exhaust Leak Path
ERR-EL-007.mechanical_failure_mode: Pre-O2 exhaust leak admitting atmospheric air into the exhaust stream between cylinder pulses via the venturi effect. Upstream O2 sensor reads false-lean, driving positive fuel trim that over-fuels the engine. The gas analyser sees raw fuel + diluted O2 as a partial-burn (inco...
ui_remediation_steps: Cold-engine listening test: a sharp ticking noise that is synchronised with cylinder firing and diminishes as the engine warms confirms a manifold-area exhaust leak.
Smoke test via the tailpipe with the engine off: smoke escaping at any pre-O2 joint, gasket, or crack confirms the leak path directly.
Exhaust analyser probe: sniff each exhaust joint and manifold runner for HC trace while the engine is running. HC detection at a joint confirms combustion gas escape before the O2 sensor.
Check LTFT for positive offset (> +10%) — the ECU's false-lean correction is the tell that the leak is upstream of the O2 sensor.
Repair the identified leak: replace the gasket, weld the crack, or tighten the flange hardware as appropriate. Replace hardware if corroded or stretched.
Verify repair: O2 sensor switching pattern returns to normal, fuel trims stabilise within +/-10%, gas analyser chemistry normalises, no exhaust noise at the repair point.
